phases.title: Establish a bounded compatibility question
phases.idea: If the project freezes its reference question, semantic boundaries, and dependency agreements before broad implementation, later differences can be attributed rather than negotiated after every test.
phases.plateau: P0: a reviewable profile and bounded development spine.
phases.falsifier: If the reference cannot be reproduced or the selected corpus cannot be bounded, revise the first profile before claiming a conformance baseline.

steps.title: Select the reference and useful scene tranche
steps.question: Which exact behaviour is the project reproducing? The answer fixes the oracle, feature inventory, and admissible release claims.

tasks.title: Record the immutable reference profile and compatibility-policy ADR.
tasks.success: The approved record identifies the reference commit/build, includes, frame/seed policy, and deliberate differences; a branch name alone fails admission.

tasks.title: Create the initial scene and feature inventory.
tasks.success: Each selected scene names its capabilities, hgpovray-specific needs, assets, and expected checkpoints; unsupported scope cannot disappear from the report.

tasks.title: Record provenance and redistribution decisions for reference material.
tasks.success: Every copied source/fixture/asset class has a recorded permission basis or a local-only acquisition route; unresolved material is excluded from distribution.

steps.title: Ratify semantic and supporting-library boundaries
steps.question: Can each subsystem evolve without changing the meaning of its neighbours? The decisions determine the first public ports and which upstream capabilities must exist before adoption.

tasks.title: Record the scene ownership and syntax/evaluation cooperation ADRs.
tasks.success: Review confirms acyclic package directions, retained macro fragments, and a neutral driver/syntax seam; no scene-to-renderer dependency appears.

tasks.title: Create a pinned Combobulate/Statelet capability agreement and consumer-fixture map.
tasks.success: CB1–CB4 and ST1–ST3 identify proposed versus implemented capabilities, acceptance owners, public consumer fixtures, adoption gates, and rollback paths; upstream releases do not depend on a full Trasic release.

tasks.title: Record numeric, resource, proof-scope, and comprehension acceptance policies.
tasks.success: Policies pre-register comparison units and limits, I01–I12 evidence methods, budgets, and reviewer tasks; unknown numerical or cost facts cannot count as certified.

steps.title: Create a bounded reproducible development spine
steps.question: Can the agreed boundaries compile and run inexpensive checks without dragging the reference renderer into production? This establishes the packaging and cost control for every slice.

tasks.title: Bootstrap the eight-crate workspace with production/development separation.
tasks.success: A dependency-graph gate rejects cycles and forbidden edges; scene/SDL builds exclude Polars and the C++ oracle; conformance remains development-only.

tasks.title: Add bounded build, reference-artefact, and documentation gates.
tasks.success: Local and CI entry points share pinned tools and declared limits; trusted reference binaries and caches avoid routine rebuilds, and heavy jobs require explicit bounded invocation.

phases.title: Inspect and compare conceptual scenes without an SDL frontend
phases.idea: If hand-built scenes and a narrow reference exporter agree under a mutation-tested comparison contract, language work can target an independently observable meaning instead of debugging through images.
phases.plateau: P1: validated scene input, inspection, and semantic comparison.
phases.falsifier: If a feature cannot be represented completely at the chosen checkpoint, mark it incomplete and add a probe or narrow the profile; do not normalize it away.

steps.title: Make scene meaning independently constructible
steps.question: Can a caller create and inspect the minimum scene without parsing source or preparing a renderer? The answer stabilizes the target for later language lowering.

tasks.title: Implement the minimal camera/sphere/material scene schema and checked domain values.
tasks.success: A hand-built scene round-trips all admitted fields; constructors reject dangling references, invalid transforms, and incomplete required data; include positive and seeded-invalid witnesses.

tasks.title: Implement finalization and validated-scene inspection/dump commands.
tasks.success: Scene input produces a deterministic versioned dump without an SDL parser; invalid or unknown-schema input cannot reach a renderable scene.

steps.title: Expose a trustworthy reference projection
steps.question: Which source checkpoint and fields expose the same minimum scene? The result determines whether scene comparison can serve as the primary language oracle.

tasks.title: Add a reference checkpoint inventory and opt-in instrumentation control.
tasks.success: Source inspection identifies the actual hook and every admitted field; instrumented/uninstrumented positive runs retain behaviour, and uncovered constructs have explicit status.

tasks.title: Implement the minimum C++ semantic exporter with reproducibility metadata.
tasks.success: The pinned reference emits camera, sphere, material, settings, and coverage with valid source/build hashes; repeated runs expose stable raw semantic data without hidden RNG or scene mutation.

steps.title: Make agreement distinguishable from missing evidence
steps.question: Can the runner expose real differences while refusing incomplete or broken evidence? Its answer authorizes the first semantic acceptance claims.

tasks.title: Implement exact semantic canonicalization and reference-preserving ID mapping.
tasks.success: Idempotence and permitted-renaming properties hold; transform, child-order, material, and resource mutations remain distinguishable.

tasks.title: Implement policy-driven numerical comparison and semantic-path diagnostics.
tasks.success: The report separates exact field mismatch from numerical closeness, names quantity policy and location, and rejects missing/non-finite data outside the profile.

tasks.title: Deliver the compare command and oracle-falsification E2E suite.
tasks.success: A positive pair agrees; seeded field omission, stale pin, malformed output, process failure, and real semantic changes produce the intended non-passing result classes.

phases.title: Render a literal scene through checked boundaries
phases.idea: If one literal scene reaches a matching conceptual scene and a correctly reconstructed image through independently checked kernels, Trasic delivers an end-to-end renderer before programmable scene generation or rich materials.
phases.plateau: P2: source-to-scene-to-image for the declared literal subset.
phases.falsifier: If an image matches but scene or component probes fail, stop acceptance at the first failed boundary; adjust the implementation rather than the reference expectation.

steps.title: Lower a literal scene with trustworthy source origins
steps.question: Can the simplest source exercise the finalization target without embedding rendering in parsing? This establishes the language seam for later macro and control-flow work.

tasks.title: Implement source storage, Logos tokens, and byte-accurate diagnostics.
tasks.success: Selected number/string/comment/encoding fixtures preserve spans and bytes; lexical errors terminate or make bounded progress rather than silently dropping input.

tasks.title: Implement expression syntax and the literal camera/sphere/material grammar.
tasks.success: Precedence and context fixtures match the selected subset; unsupported constructs receive explicit diagnostics; macro bodies remain extensible token fragments rather than an incompatible expression-only model.

tasks.title: Implement literal evaluation, ordered transforms, and scene lowering.
tasks.success: Literal source produces the same admitted scene fields as the reference, including defaults and transform order; failure retains original source and does not finalize a partial scene.

steps.title: Establish independent camera, surface, and light responses
steps.question: Do the smallest rendering components obey their own contracts? Independent probes distinguish geometric, texture, and transport errors before final image comparison.

tasks.title: Implement sphere queries with explicit ray-parameter and normal contracts.
tasks.success: Analytic and reference probes cover misses, tangencies, inside origins, non-unit directions, and supported transforms; solver failures do not masquerade as misses.

tasks.title: Implement the selected perspective camera ray generator.
tasks.success: Centre/corner and transformed-camera rays match reference probes under the declared camera convention, independently of material or transport code.

tasks.title: Implement constant-pigment/material sampling through the texture port.
tasks.success: Independent context probes preserve all admitted colour/material fields and reject unavailable resources or unsupported material tags rather than substituting defaults.

tasks.title: Implement bounded direct illumination, visibility, and background transport.
tasks.success: Small visibility and light-response fixtures match component/reference expectations with explicit work limits; the transport port remains callable without SDL.

steps.title: Complete the first composed tile and image path
steps.question: Can the first real rendering slice exercise Combobulate without hiding scalar semantics or film effects? The result determines the minimum typed native adapter contract.

tasks.title: Implement the minimum public Combobulate sample-grid and ray-batch adapter.
tasks.success: The actually available pinned typed/native contract preserves sample identity for empty/singleton/tile batches; public-only fixtures pass and no unimplemented API is assumed.
tasks.upstream: Combobulate CB1 and the required minimum of CB3.

tasks.title: Implement tile-local reconstruction, one-time commit, and the render command.
tasks.success: A literal scene renders through the CLI; weighted output follows the declared initial filter; pre-commit failure leaves the tile unchanged and reports prior commits accurately.

tasks.title: Add literal-scene E2E comparison across scene, component, and image checkpoints.
tasks.success: The same fixtures pass required scene and component gates before image acceptance; mutations in camera, geometry, pigment, and encoding localize to their first relevant boundary.

phases.title: Execute reusable scene programs with attributable state changes
phases.idea: If declarations, expansion, includes, and bounded control flow preserve the same scene meaning while observations preserve behaviour, the language architecture scales beyond literal examples without becoming opaque.
phases.plateau: P3: reusable scene source with bounded evaluation and structured diagnostics.
phases.falsifier: If fragment macros require a parallel parser or tracing changes evaluation, revise the seam or observation contract before extending the language surface.

steps.title: Support stateful expansion without package cycles
steps.question: Can language execution supply context-sensitive input while syntax remains reusable? The answer validates the cooperative driver before broad directive coverage.

tasks.title: Implement the syntax/evaluation request driver and expansion-frame lifecycle.
tasks.success: A public-boundary fixture suspends/resumes syntax without overlapping retained mutable borrows; progress and frame unwinding controls reject looping or stale continuations.

tasks.title: Implement declarations, local bindings, and admitted value coercions.
tasks.success: Scope shadowing, copy/reference behaviour, and coercion fixtures match the pinned reference; emitted object meaning changes only when the selected semantics permit it.

tasks.title: Implement parameterized macros including surrounding-grammar token fragments.
tasks.success: Nested and fragment-producing macros compare at scene level; definition/invocation provenance survives; recursion and generated-token limits reject nonterminating expansion.

steps.title: Add resource-aware reusable control flow
steps.question: Can scene programmes reuse files and control construction without hidden I/O or unbounded work? The outcome fixes the host capability boundary.

tasks.title: Implement includes through frozen-source and authorized-resource ports.
tasks.success: Nested include scope and source chains match the profile; traversal, symlink-policy, changed-file, and cycle/depth cases fail under the declared policy.

tasks.title: Implement conditional directives with reference-matched inactive-text behaviour.
tasks.success: Inactive branches do not read assets, consume RNG, mutate bindings, or emit objects; lexical/structural rejection follows the pinned profile rather than an eager AST assumption.

tasks.title: Implement bounded loop replay and explicit frame/seed inputs.
tasks.success: Loop and expansion work is charged before growth; fixed input environments reproduce results; nested limits and repeated empty-body loops cannot escape admission.

steps.title: Observe evaluation without owning or changing it
steps.question: Can Statelet expose a useful explanation without altering state, ownership, or effects? The evidence decides which synchronous contracts Trasic adopts.

tasks.title: Add synchronous capture and caller-context integration at evaluation transitions.
tasks.success: Enabled/disabled controls preserve result/state/effects under documented callback assumptions; capture counts, short borrows, and filtered-child isolation hold.
tasks.upstream: Statelet RFCs 0001–0003, conditional on accepted contracts or reviewed handwritten conventions.

tasks.title: Add scoped structured recording, stable outcome names, and incomplete-completion reporting.
tasks.success: Parallel recorders remain isolated; late fields reach the correct observation; enum renames do not change semantic names; missing completion never implies cancellation or success.
tasks.upstream: Statelet RFCs 0004–0005 and ADR 005; synchronous scope only.

tasks.title: Deliver programmable-scene interaction and diagnostic E2E fixtures.
tasks.success: Macro/include/local/conditional/loop combinations produce equivalent scenes or declared rejections, with minimized failures and attributable transition/source context.

phases.title: Render admitted CSG and textured materials without losing provenance
phases.idea: If additional primitives, CSG, and materials extend the existing contracts without flattening boundary provenance or hiding coordinate policy, Trasic can support richer selected scenes without a second renderer architecture.
phases.plateau: P4: the admitted geometric and material interactions render with independent evidence.
phases.falsifier: If coincident surfaces or texture transforms require unexplained tolerances, keep those cases outside support until the reference-backed rule is explicit.

steps.title: Extend geometry through the existing query contract
steps.question: Do new primitives and transformations preserve the same observable ray and normal semantics? The answer provides the event inputs for CSG.

tasks.title: Add plane descriptions, lowering, reference export, and geometry queries.
tasks.success: Literal plane scenes compare and render through existing ports; parallel/inside/boundary cases follow the profile and preserve material provenance.

tasks.title: Add box descriptions, lowering, reference export, and geometry queries.
tasks.success: Box slabs, edge/corner ties, inside rays, and non-unit directions match independent probes without a special renderer path.

tasks.title: Complete the admitted affine transformation and normal/orientation surface.
tasks.success: Ordered, nonuniform, and negative transforms preserve parameter mapping and inverse-transpose normal policy; metamorphic and reference controls detect wrong multiplication/order or normalization.

steps.title: Retain CSG event and material meaning
steps.question: Can Boolean solids preserve inside state, ties, orientation, and material ownership? This determines whether segmented composition later has a trustworthy domain control.

tasks.title: Add explicit per-ray events and the admitted union contract.
tasks.success: The schema/exporter and scalar event path preserve child identity, initial inside state, contact/crossing distinctions, and the selected union behaviour.

tasks.title: Add intersection and difference with explicit coincident-event policy.
tasks.success: Selected nested solids preserve boundary normal and material provenance; coincident/tangent events use the recorded reference rule rather than blind toggling or pairwise-epsilon sorting.

tasks.title: Add CSG reference-query and interaction fixtures across admitted primitives.
tasks.success: Targeted operation/transform/tie/material combinations match independent reference events and visible-hit selection; event-order and provenance mutations fail.

steps.title: Add texture and transport features as observable scene extensions
steps.question: Can richer appearance reuse scene and sampling boundaries without silently changing colour or material semantics? The result expands the useful profile one feature at a time.

tasks.title: Add checker pigments and explicit texture transformations.
tasks.success: Point/context probes and scene dumps preserve checker boundaries and object-versus-texture transform order; no image-only acceptance.

tasks.title: Add one approved image-map decoding, coordinate, and filtering path.
tasks.success: Resource hashes, decoding limits, wrap/edge/filter behaviour, and colour transfer match the declared mode; unsupported modes fail explicitly.

tasks.title: Add the selected bounded reflection contribution.
tasks.success: Component and image fixtures establish reflection/material behaviour with depth/work limits; cancellation and budget rejection do not expose a partial tile.

tasks.title: Add the selected refraction/interior contribution and material fields.
tasks.success: Admitted entry/exit and total-internal-reflection cases match reference policy; interior, filter, transmission, and normal orientation remain distinct and attributable.

tasks.title: Deliver CSG/texture/transport E2E interaction coverage.
tasks.success: The richer source tranche passes scene, domain, and image gates; combinations include nested solids, transformed textures, resource changes, and material provenance.

phases.title: Deliver bounded packet, segment, and tile composition
phases.idea: If Combobulate preserves domain meaning, logical identity, and bounded effects on demanding rendering work while making review no harder, its abstraction delivers application value beyond a literal demonstration.
phases.plateau: P5: the three composition experiments have reproducible evidence and accepted contracts.
phases.falsifier: If a route changes meaning, executes inactive work, hides allocations, or fails pre-registered review/resource criteria, revise the adapter or upstream contract and rerun the affected experiment.

steps.title: Prove packet execution is a faithful domain adapter
steps.question: Can a reusable native plan batch the existing geometry without changing identities or numerical contracts? The outcome decides packet sizing and the public adapter shape.

tasks.title: Implement reusable packet plans with genuine masking and explicit correspondence.
tasks.success: Forced inactive faulting cells do not execute; empty/singleton/reordered packets preserve ray IDs and query outcomes; the plan explains actual native/backend boundaries.

tasks.title: Add public-only layout, bounds, and proof-capable consumer bindings.
tasks.success: Actual accepted public contracts bind to production execution; owned index/shape checks have scoped evidence, reachable success, and rejecting stale-witness/always-error controls; no verifier is required for normal use.
tasks.upstream: Combobulate CB4; use the agreed supported Kani/Verus subset rather than claiming universal geometry proofs.

tasks.title: Run and publish the packet-geometry comparison experiment.
tasks.success: Record separate setup/preparation/execution/copy/allocation costs and reviewer results against pre-registered criteria; adapter parity and independent geometric correctness are reported as different claims.

steps.title: Compose CSG over identity-preserving segments
steps.question: Do collection abstractions preserve the scalar CSG contract across empty and variably sized per-ray event lists? The answer fixes segment ownership and tie-policy seams.

tasks.title: Implement the public segmented-event adapter around Trasic-owned CSG policy.
tasks.success: Validated offsets and per-ray identity survive empty segments, compaction, and chunking; CSG ties and material selection stay in domain code.

tasks.title: Run and publish the segmented-CSG comparison experiment.
tasks.success: Scalar and composed paths agree with the selected domain/reference evidence on ties, tangencies, nesting, provenance, and partition variants; failure yields a recorded contract revision.

steps.title: Compose complete tiles with bounded effects
steps.question: Can preparation, sampling, reconstruction, and accumulation form a legible plan without changing sample streams or exposing partial commits? The outcome determines the production tile execution contract.

tasks.title: Implement weighted-splat reconstruction with an explicit reducer and indexed sink.
tasks.success: Sample IDs, weights, collision order, and normalization survive filtering and regrouping permitted by policy; a generic mean or duplicated commit fails controls.

tasks.title: Add bounded tile scheduling, dynamic admission, and cancellation-safe commit reporting.
tasks.success: Checked work/storage growth and declared concurrency limits apply before allocation; injected cancellation before/after commit produces correct destination and completion status.

tasks.title: Run and publish the complete-tile experiment and configuration interaction suite.
tasks.success: Report numerical and sample-identity agreement, peak tracked/untracked memory, stage costs, and independent reviewer outcomes across accepted tile/worker/backend/observation combinations.

phases.title: Publish an honest supported profile and reproducible evidence
phases.idea: If support declarations, executable evidence, and operational limits agree on the same frozen profile, users can reproduce the claims and maintainers can extend it without erasing uncertainty.
phases.plateau: P6: a release candidate with named supported scope and verifiable evidence.
phases.falsifier: If required features remain uncovered or a reference/tool change invalidates evidence, the release gate stays closed; reduce scope only through an explicit owner-approved profile revision.

steps.title: Close the feature and interaction coverage contract
steps.question: Does the implemented feature set actually serve the selected hgpovray tranche? The answer defines the release label and any additional work that must precede it.

tasks.title: Reconcile the selected scene tranche with implementation/exporter capability coverage.
tasks.success: Every required field and feature has implementation and oracle evidence; missing fork-specific needs generate explicit review-sized tasks before this gate can pass, rather than a blanket compatibility claim.

tasks.title: Deliver the supported-profile E2E and targeted combinatorial suite.
tasks.success: All required fixtures run under frozen policies; dangerous high-order interactions have explicit coverage and deliberate semantic faults fail at the appropriate checkpoint.

tasks.title: Implement profile/schema/dependency migration and stale-evidence rejection.
tasks.success: Changed schema, numerical policy, executable binding, or asset/reference pin invalidates affected evidence; a reviewed migration records actual semantic changes without blindly replacing snapshots.

steps.title: Make supported use and validation reproducible
steps.question: Can another maintainer reproduce the claimed behaviour with the documented commands, resources, and assumptions? This establishes release usability rather than merely a passing development machine.

tasks.title: Complete the CLI/library usage, diagnostics, and supported-feature documentation.
tasks.success: Fresh-environment instructions reproduce check/dump/render/compare/probe workflows; exit codes, limits, redaction, and partial-output policy match actual behaviour.

tasks.title: Record independent comprehension and operating-cost acceptance results.
tasks.success: Named participants complete the registered localization/review tasks; measured build/prover/runtime/storage costs meet the approved limits or trigger an explicit unaccepted finding.

tasks.title: Assemble and validate the release evidence bundle.
tasks.success: The bundle binds production source, reference/exporter, corpus, policies, dependencies, proof scopes, positive witnesses, negative controls, and residual gaps; another maintainer can reproduce the required gates.

steps.title: Ratify the release claim without erasing exclusions
steps.question: What exactly may this release claim? The decision controls publication and the baseline for later profiles.

tasks.title: Record the supported-profile acceptance decision and release exclusions.
tasks.success: The owner accepts a precisely named profile with zero unclassified required mismatches and explicit unsupported/partial scope; absent evidence cannot receive a completed compatibility label.

phases.title: Evaluate extensions without destabilizing the accepted profile
phases.idea: If the core profile is already reproducible, wider features and execution strategies can be judged by concrete scene value and independent evidence instead of expanding the initial promise by inertia.
phases.plateau: Deferred options only; these tasks are not prerequisites of P6.
phases.falsifier: An extension without a concrete consumer, bounded validation route, or acceptable resource model remains deferred. Full historical compatibility stays a non-goal.

steps.title: Admit further language and hgpovray capabilities through explicit profiles
steps.question: Which additional scene needs justify a new semantic contract? The answer determines extension-specific ADRs and delivery slices, not an automatic widening of v0.1.

tasks.title: Define an evidence-backed next-profile tranche for additional primitives, patterns, or media.
tasks.success: Named scenes justify each capability; an exporter/query plan and resource budget exist before implementation tasks enter the active roadmap.

tasks.title: Design retained user functions and scene-time query integration for a selected consumer.
tasks.success: A typed inspectable function/query contract preserves evaluation-time distinctions and acyclic packaging; no opaque serialized closure or speculative generic VM enters the core.

steps.title: Evaluate acceleration and alternate execution under the same semantics
steps.question: Which measured bottleneck warrants a new execution structure? The result decides whether additional complexity earns a maintained production path.

tasks.title: Add a conservative BVH only after a recorded workload justifies it.
tasks.success: The accepted workload shows the need; generated and adversarial queries establish no missing required hits against the bounded brute-force control, with measured construction and traversal costs.

tasks.title: Prototype an explicitly scoped GPU, JIT, wavefront, or distributed route.
tasks.success: A separate design selects one route and states semantic/numerical/sampler/commit differences; representative evidence meets pre-registered criteria before promotion.

steps.title: Expand observation and platform claims only with new evidence
steps.question: Do actual async or platform needs justify additional guarantees? The answer determines separate conformance matrices and upstream work.

tasks.title: Evaluate asynchronous observation and cancellation on an actual async consumer.
tasks.success: The upstream async gate and real Trasic need both exist; cancellation, incomplete completion, and callback lifetimes have separate evidence without retroactively claiming synchronous tests proved them.
tasks.upstream: Statelet RFC 0005 and the separately gated async roadmap.

tasks.title: Qualify an additional platform or numerical/backend profile.
tasks.success: A separately identified build and policy pass the required corpus and resource controls; results do not imply universal bitwise parity or silently replace the original profile.
